was: Rotary Club of Grande Prairie campground, built from 1967 on land the city provided; all of its profits go back into the community.  It has 21 full-service 30-amp sites, 16 power-and-water 50-amp pull-throughs and 24 power-and-water back-ins (20 of them 30-amp and 4 50-amp), and the section of sites 22 to 41 has fire pits (except at 34) and a playground.  A grocery store and a casino are across the street, and the Muskoseepi Park walking trails are at hand.  No tents; bookings for the Bear Creek Folk Festival weekend are non-refundable. --Claude

was: Regional park in the South Saskatchewan River valley south of Eston, beside the river, with an irrigated nine-hole grass-greens golf course and licensed clubhouse, an outdoor pool, mini golf, two ball diamonds, a playground and a hall to rent; the pool and concession open in July and August.  It has 18 full-service sites, 20 15-amp electric sites and 10 non-serviced sites plus group camping; every site has a picnic table and a pole barbecue or fire pit.  The campground taps are not drinking water, which is sold at the clubhouse and concession.  There is no boat launch (the nearest is at the ferry, about 10 km away), but boats can be beached beside the park. --Claude

was: Regional park on the shores of Nickle Lake and the Souris River near Weyburn, where tall poplars line the road in and each area has a playground; there are shelters and benches along the shoreline, a groomed sandy beach and roped-off swimming area (no lifeguard), an 18-hole mini golf course and, new in 2026, a canteen.  Its 342 sites are 16 tent, 55 full-service and 271 30-amp power-and-water sites, with group camping in a secluded bay and at Crescent Point; some partial-service sites in Riverview are pull-throughs.  Two boat launches and a floating dock serve the lake, which holds walleye, perch and pike, is stocked from time to time and has a fish-cleaning area.  An 18-hole golf course is 3 miles away. --Claude

was: Regional park at Wynyard's west entrance, 2.5 km south of the Yellowhead Highway on Grid 640, quiet and well treed; its reservoir, behind the old CPR dam, is aerated and holds rainbow trout (canoes, kayaks and electric boats only; fishing needs a provincial licence).  Campers have barbecues and free firewood; the park's water is not drinkable, and a coin-operated potable water station is at the Town Shop in Wynyard.  There is no full-time attendant: the facilities are cleaned and restocked once a day.  Camping runs from the Victoria Day long weekend to the end of September, and the trails stay open all year. --Claude

was: Working cattle ranch of Ben Mead and his daughter Carla in Nine Mile Canyon, 24 paved miles up Nine Mile Canyon Road from Wellington and a gateway to the canyon's petroglyphs; its campgrounds are the only camping allowed in the canyon.  The sites lie along Nine Mile Creek amid shade and green grass, each with a picnic table and fire ring, and every campground has a spring-water faucet; Kokopelli is best for RVs, trailers and vans, Cottonwood Hollow mostly for tents and small vans, and the Turnouts are pull-throughs.  Showers ($3) are at the main ranch, and generators are off from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. (9 p.m. in fall).  The ranch also rents settler cabins rebuilt on the property and bed-and-breakfast rooms.  There is no cell service in the 50-mile canyon, and Wi-Fi only around the main house. --Claude
note: Working cattle ranch of Ben Mead and his daughter Carla in Nine Mile Canyon, 24 paved miles up Nine Mile Canyon Road from Wellington and a gateway to the canyon's petroglyphs; its campgrounds are the only camping allowed in the canyon.  Its campgrounds sit beside Nine Mile Creek with plenty of shade and green grass; every site has a picnic table and a fire pit or ring, and every campground a spring-water faucet.  Kokopelli is best for RVs, trailers and vans, Cottonwood Hollow is mostly for tents, small vans and truck campers, and the Turnouts are pull-throughs.  Showers ($3) are at the main ranch, and generators are off from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. (9 p.m. in fall).  The ranch also rents settler cabins rebuilt on the property and bed-and-breakfast rooms.  There is no cell service in the 50-mile canyon, and Wi-Fi only around the main house. --Claude

Kayaking and windsurfing on the lake are popular. --Claude

was: Lewis County PUD campground at Leonard “Bud” Allen Park, over 110 acres, 15 miles east of Morton and central to Mount St. Helens, Mount Rainier and the Gifford Pinchot National Forest.  It has 41 RV sites with electric and water hookups in Areas A and D, 21 tent sites, 6 group tent sites and a group RV site, plus picnic shelters, barbecues, baseball, soccer and volleyball, disc golf, horseshoes, nature trails, a playground and a boat launch.  The dump station is for registered campers only, and RV chemicals must not be used in holding tanks (the campground is on a septic system).  The gates are open from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.; a 25% disability discount is given with a placard or pass. --Claude

was: Family-owned RV and tent resort in the heart of Westport, close to the beaches, parks, restaurants, shops, marina and docks; it has a 2,400 sq ft clubhouse to rent, a secluded tent area, three rental cabins, a fish-cleaning station, a heated outdoor pool, horseshoe pits, a playground and campfire containers, and sells propane, ice and firewood.  Monthly rates are offered by phone. --Claude
